subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Io: The Volcanic Moon
description: A quick, practical guide to Io: The Volcanic Moon.

hook.text: Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active body in the solar system—over 400 active volcanoes dot its surface.

buildup.text: Tidal forces from Jupiter and neighboring moons constantly squeeze Io, generating intense internal heat.

discovery.text: Voyager 1 caught an eruption in 1979—the first active volcanism seen beyond Earth. Plumes rose 300 km high.

twist.text: Io's surface is constantly resurfaced by lava flows. There are no impact craters—they're buried under fresh lava.

climax.text: Some eruptions produce lava hotter than anything on Earth today—possibly reaching 1,700°C, similar to early Earth.

punchline.text: Four hundred volcanoes. No craters. The solar system's most restless world.

quiz.question: What makes Io so volcanically active?
options: Tidal forces from Jupiter and neighboring moons generate intense internal heat
Io has a radioactive core that produces far more heat than other moons
Solar radiation heats Io's thin atmosphere, triggering eruptions

details.summary: Io, Jupiter's innermost large moon, is the most volcanically active body in the solar system. Gravitational tidal forces from Jupiter and neighboring moons continuously knead Io's interior, generating enormous heat that drives hundreds of active volcanoes.
details.whyItMatters: Io demonstrates that tidal heating can drive extreme geological activity without sunlight or radioactive decay alone. It's a living laboratory for understanding volcanism and tidal interactions across the solar system.
takeaways: Most volcanically active body in the solar system
Tidal heating from Jupiter drives hundreds of active volcanoes
Sulfur plumes reach 500 km above the surface

faq.question: Why is Io so volcanically active?
faq.answer: Jupiter's enormous gravity, combined with orbital resonances with Europa and Ganymede, continuously deforms Io like a kneaded ball. This tidal flexing generates tremendous internal friction and heat — an estimated 100 trillion watts.

faq.question: What are Io's volcanoes like?
faq.answer: Io has over 400 known volcanic centers. Some produce thin, flowing lava; others create enormous plumes of sulfur and sulfur dioxide gas. Loki Patera, Io's largest active volcanic feature, is a 200-km lava lake. Temperatures at eruption sites can exceed 1,600°C — hotter than anything on Earth.
